In Jewish culture, the crowing of the rooster symbolizes the beginning of a new day, but here it becomes a symbol of Peter's failure to remain faithful. This detail emphasizes Jesus' forewarning and the certainty of His announcement, reinforcing the idea that even moments of human weakness can be foreseen by God. It reminds us that God knows our struggles and failures even before they occur.

34.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the last week of Jesus' life, shortly before His crucifixion, a period marked by increasing tensions between Jesus and the Jewish religious authorities.
34.passage: In Matthew 26, Jesus prepares His disciples for His imminent arrest. This chapter addresses themes of betrayal, loyalty, and human nature in the face of trial.
34.culture: At that time, denial was considered an act of great shame, especially for a disciple. The crowing of the rooster was a culturally recognized signal, adding a dramatic dimension to Jesus' prophecy.
34.interpretation: This verse illustrates human weakness and divine foresight. It highlights the fact that even those who are close to Jesus can fail, but this does not diminish God's love and grace towards them.
34.commentaire: This passage reminds us that we are all susceptible to failing in our faith. However, just like Peter, we have the opportunity to return to Jesus, who offers forgiveness and redemption. It is essential to remain vigilant and seek strength in Christ so as not to succumb to the trials of life.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to deny' or 'to disown'. It is composed of 'ἀπό' (from) and 'ἀρνέομαι' (to deny). In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the seriousness of betrayal and Peter's commitment not to deny his Lord, even in the face of death. Spiritually, this evokes the struggle between faithfulness and fear, a central theme in the Christian life.

This word means 'death'. It is often used in the New Testament to refer not only to physical death but also to spiritual separation from God. In this verse, Peter expresses a willingness to face death to remain faithful, which highlights the depth of his commitment to Christ, even though that commitment will be tested.

This term translates to 'testimony'. It is derived from 'μάρτυς' (martyr) and implies a declaration of truth, often at the cost of one's life. In the context of Peter's declaration, it underscores the willingness to bear witness to his faith, even in the most difficult moments, and reminds believers of the importance of standing firm in their testimony of Christ.

35.epoque: This passage is set in the first century, in the context of Palestine under Roman occupation, where religious and political tensions were high.
35.passage: This verse is found in the account of Jesus' Passion, where He announces to His disciples that they will deny Him. It illustrates human fragility in the face of adversity and the necessity of divine grace.
35.culture: In the Jewish culture of the time, loyalty to a master was paramount, and denial was seen as a grave betrayal. The disciples, in affirming their commitment, show their desire to remain faithful despite threatening circumstances.
35.interpretation: Peter, in asserting that he will not deny Jesus, expresses a self-confidence that will be tested. This reminds us that even the most fervent believers can falter under pressure, and that our strength comes from our dependence on God.
35.commentaire: This verse encourages us to recognize our own weakness and the necessity of God's grace. Like Peter, we may have good intentions, but we must rely on prayer and communion with the Holy Spirit to remain faithful in trials. Let us be vigilant and humble, knowing that our strength lies in our relationship with Christ.

mots.sens: The term 'Gethsemane' literally means 'olive press'. This place is symbolic of the pressure and suffering that Jesus was about to endure. In the spiritual context, it also represents the place of submission to God's will, where Jesus prepares for His ultimate sacrifice. This word evokes a depth of suffering and devotion, highlighting Christ's humanity in the face of His destiny.

This verb means 'to pray' and implies a deep communication with God. In the context of this verse, it underscores the importance of prayer in times of distress and decision. Prayer is an act of dependence and seeking divine strength, and here it highlights the intimate relationship between Jesus and His Father, especially in moments of crisis.

The word 'mathētai' translates to 'disciples' and refers to those who follow and learn from Jesus. This underscores the importance of the community of believers and their role in Jesus' ministry. Their presence in this crucial moment reminds us that even disciples must learn to pray and support, but also to understand the depth of commitment to God.

36.epoque: This passage is set in the first century, in the context of Roman-occupied Palestine, where religious and political tensions were palpable. Jesus, as the central figure of nascent Christianity, prepares to face crucifixion, a defining event in the history of humanity.
36.passage: In Matthew 26, we are on the eve of Jesus' crucifixion. This chapter highlights Jesus' last moments with His disciples, where He teaches, prepares, and withdraws to pray before facing His passion. This moment in Gethsemane is crucial as it reveals Jesus' inner struggle and His need for communion with the Father.
36.culture: In Jewish culture, prayer is a central act of spiritual life, often associated with moments of crisis or need. The garden of Gethsemane is a place of reflection and prayer, a sacred space where one withdraws to seek God's will, which was a common practice among Jews of the time.
36.interpretation: This verse illustrates Jesus' vulnerability in the face of impending suffering while affirming His commitment to pray. It shows that even the Son of God needs moments of solitude and prayer to be strengthened. It also reminds us that prayer is essential in our own lives, especially in difficult times.
36.commentaire: Jesus, by withdrawing to pray, teaches us the importance of prayer in our lives, especially when we face trials. This moment in Gethsemane reminds us that communion with God is essential to find strength and direction. As disciples, we must learn to sit in prayer, seek the Lord, and prepare to face our own challenges with faith.

mots.sens: This word means 'sorrow' or 'grief.' It evokes a deep emotional pain, often related to loss or suffering. In this context, it emphasizes the state of anguish that Jesus feels in light of his imminent sacrifice. Spiritually, it reminds us that even the Son of God experienced moments of profound sadness, making his sacrifice even more poignant for humanity.

The term 'agony' refers to an intense struggle, often associated with fear or anxiety. It is derived from a root meaning 'struggle' or 'combat,' and in this passage, it highlights Jesus' inner struggle as he faces his destiny. Theologically, this teaches us that Jesus fully experienced the human condition, including fear and anguish, which makes him perfectly able to understand our own struggles.

This verb means 'to take with oneself' or 'to receive.' In this context, it indicates that Jesus chooses to share this crucial moment with his disciples, Peter and the sons of Zebedee. This action underscores the importance of community and support in times of distress, and theologically, it reminds us that Jesus does not abandon us in our trials.

37.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the 1st century, during a time when Palestine was under Roman occupation, and where religious and political tensions were high. Jesus' disciples were facing a period of uncertainty and imminent danger for their master.
37.passage: In this chapter, Jesus prepares for his arrest and crucifixion. He takes his disciples with him to pray in the Garden of Gethsemane, a crucial moment where he faces his destiny. This passage illustrates Jesus' inner struggle before bearing the weight of the sins of the world.
37.culture: In the Jewish culture of the time, prayer and community support were essential, especially in times of crisis. The disciples were called to watch and pray with Jesus, highlighting the importance of solidarity in faith.
37.interpretation: This verse shows the humanity of Jesus, who experiences deep emotions such as sadness and anguish. It reminds us that God understands our sufferings and struggles, as he has experienced them himself. The presence of the disciples also underscores the importance of community in difficult times.
37.commentaire: This passage teaches us that even in moments of great distress, we are not alone. Jesus, by sharing his anguish with his disciples, shows us the importance of prayer and mutual support. In our own struggles, we can turn to God and to others for comfort and strength.

mots.sens: This term refers to the soul or the inner life of the individual. In the biblical context, it represents the immaterial part of man, often associated with his emotions and will. Here, Jesus expresses a deep distress, highlighting the inner struggle he feels before his crucifixion, reminding us of the humanity of Christ and the anguish faced in suffering.

This word means pressure, affliction, or distress. It evokes a situation of intense suffering, both physical and spiritual. In this verse, Jesus' sadness is an anticipation of the anguish he is about to experience, illustrating the depth of his sacrifice and his solidarity with our human suffering.

This verb means to watch or to stay awake. It implies active vigilance, often in a context of prayer or preparation. Jesus asks his disciples to watch with him, emphasizing the importance of prayer during times of trial, and calls us to remain attentive to our own spiritual lives.

38.epoque: This passage is set at the end of Jesus' earthly ministry, just before his crucifixion, during a time when the tension between the religious authorities and Jesus reaches its peak.
38.passage: In Matthew chapter 26, Jesus announces his imminent death and shares a last meal with his disciples. This verse is found in the Garden of Gethsemane, where he prepares to face his ultimate sacrifice.
38.culture: In Jewish culture, the garden represents a place of prayer and communion with God. The fact that Jesus asks his disciples to watch with him underscores the importance of community and mutual support in times of distress.
38.interpretation: By expressing his sadness, Jesus shows that he has fully shared our humanity, including our emotional struggles. This passage reminds us that even in our darkest moments, we are not alone and that we can turn to God and to others for support.
38.commentaire: This verse invites us to reflect on our own spiritual lives and how we support those who are going through trials. By watching and praying, we can prepare to face our own challenges with the strength that God provides. Let us be attentive to the needs of those around us and remember to pray for those who suffer, just as Jesus did.

mots.sens: This word means 'prayer' and comes from the root 'ευχή' (euché), which denotes a request or supplication made to God. In the context of Matthew 26:39, it emphasizes the intimacy and depth of communication between Jesus and the Father. Prayer here is an act of submission and dependence, revealing the human nature of Jesus in the face of imminent suffering.

This term denotes the will or purpose of God. It evokes not only the idea of what God desires but also the notion of accepting His divine will by believers. In this verse, Jesus expresses total submission to the Father's will, illustrating the importance of seeking and accepting God's plan even in times of great distress.

This word means 'cup,' symbolizing here the burden of suffering and the sacrifice to come. In Jewish tradition, the cup can also represent judgment or suffering. Jesus asks that this 'cup' be taken away from him, indicating the gravity of what he is about to endure, while affirming his willingness to submit to God's will.

39.epoque: This passage is set in the first century, during the earthly life of Jesus, as he prepares for his crucifixion, a central event of the Christian faith.
39.passage: Matthew 26:39 is found in the context of the Agony in the Garden of Gethsemane, where Jesus, aware of his imminent sacrifice, seeks strength in prayer while expressing his inner struggle between human fear and divine obedience.
39.culture: In Jewish culture, prayer was a fundamental act of spiritual life, often associated with moments of crisis or decision. The Garden of Gethsemane, a place of refuge, becomes the stage for Jesus' spiritual struggle.
39.interpretation: This verse illustrates the tension between Jesus' human nature, which fears suffering, and his divine obedience to the Father's will. It teaches us the importance of submitting to God's will, even when it involves personal sacrifices.
39.commentaire: Matthew 26:39 reminds us that prayer is essential in times of crisis. Like Jesus, we are called to turn to the Father, to express our fears while choosing to submit to His will. This passage encourages us to seek strength in prayer and to accept God's plan, even when it seems difficult or painful.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to awaken' or 'to rise up'. In the context of Matthew 26:40, it evokes the idea of coming out of a state of inactivity or spiritual sleep. This emphasizes the call to vigilance and prayer, which is essential for the disciples, especially in moments of distress. The theological significance here is that Jesus expects his disciples to be alert and engaged in prayer, particularly during crucial times.

This term means 'night', a period often associated with darkness and anguish. It reminds believers that times of crisis require heightened vigilance and communion with God, even when the environment seems hostile.

This word refers to 'prayer', an act of communication with God. In the context of this passage, prayer is presented as a necessity to overcome temptation and despair. 40.epoque: This passage takes place during the period of Jesus' earthly ministry, just before his crucifixion, a time of intense tension for him and his disciples.
40.passage: Matthew 26:40 is found in the account of Jesus' agony in the Garden of Gethsemane, where he seeks the support of his disciples in a critical moment. This chapter addresses themes of betrayal, suffering, and the necessity of prayer.
40.culture: In the Jewish culture of the time, prayer was an essential practice, especially in moments of crisis. The disciples would have understood the importance of being watchful and praying, but their physical fatigue prevented them from responding to Jesus' call.
40.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of spiritual vigilance and prayer in times of trial. Jesus, as a model, shows that even in pain, one must seek communion with God. The disciples' failure to stay awake often symbolizes our own tendency to neglect our prayer life.
40.commentaire: This passage reminds us that prayer is a powerful weapon in times of crisis. As disciples, we are called to watch and pray, not only for ourselves but also to support those who are going through trials. Spiritual vigilance is essential to remain steadfast in faith and resist the temptations that may arise in our daily lives.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to pray' and evokes a deep communication with God. In this verse, it emphasizes that prayer is essential to resist temptation, as it connects us to divine strength.

This word means 'flesh' and represents human nature, often associated with weakness and sin. In the New Testament, it is used to describe the limitations of man in contrast to the spirit. 41.epoque: This passage is set in the context of Jesus' ministry, shortly before his crucifixion, at a time when religious and political tensions were high in Israel.
41.passage: In Matthew 26, Jesus prepares for his passion and asks his disciples to watch and pray as he is distressed in the Garden of Gethsemane. This moment underscores the importance of prayer in times of crisis.
41.culture: In Jesus' time, prayer was a central practice in Jewish life, often associated with moments of distress or spiritual need. The disciples, as Jews, understood the importance of prayer, but their inability to stay awake reveals a universal human struggle.

41.commentaire: Matthew 26:41 reminds us that prayer is a powerful tool to resist temptations. By watching and praying, we align ourselves with God's will and strengthen our spirit against the attacks of the enemy. This passage urges us to recognize our human weakness and seek divine strength to live a life that honors God.

mots.sens: This term means 'father' and evokes an intimate and protective relationship. In the context of Matthew 26:42, Jesus addresses God as his Father, highlighting the depth of their relationship. This word means 'will' and refers to the divine desire or plan. In this verse, it emphasizes the importance of submitting to God's will, even when it involves personal sacrifices. God's will is often in opposition to our own desires, and recognizing this is essential for living an authentic Christian life.

This term translates to 'cup' and often symbolizes the destiny or trial one must face. 42.epoque: This passage is set in the 1st century, during the period when Jesus is preparing for his crucifixion, a crucial moment in Christian history.
42.passage: Matthew 26:42 is found in the context of Jesus' agony in the Garden of Gethsemane, where he struggles with the reality of his impending suffering while seeking to align his will with that of his Father.

42.interpretation: This verse illustrates Jesus' inner struggle between his humanity and divinity, showing that he is fully aware of the cost of his sacrifice. By submitting to God's will, he teaches us the importance of faith and obedience, even in the most difficult moments.
42.commentaire: Matthew 26:42 reminds us that prayer is a place of confrontation with our fears and desires. Like Jesus, we are called to seek God's will in our lives, even when it involves sacrifices. By accepting the cup that God presents to us, we participate in his redemptive plan and testify to our faith in his wisdom and goodness.

mots.sens: This word means 'sleep' and evokes a state of inactivity or unconsciousness. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes human weakness in the face of spiritual trial. 43.epoque: This passage is set in the 1st century, during the earthly life of Jesus, as He prepares to suffer for humanity. It is a pivotal moment in the history of salvation, where the tension between the kingdom of God and the forces of evil reaches its peak.
43.passage: In Matthew 26, Jesus is in the Garden of Gethsemane, where He faces great distress before His crucifixion. This chapter highlights the importance of prayer and spiritual struggle, contrasting Jesus' vigilance with the drowsiness of His disciples.

This reminds us of our own struggle against spiritual laziness and the importance of remaining vigilant in our faith life.
43.commentaire: This passage teaches us the necessity of spiritual vigilance. Just like the disciples, we can be distracted by the concerns of daily life and neglect our prayer life. It is essential to cultivate a constant attitude of prayer and to remain attentive to the moments when God calls us to watch and pray, especially in trials.

mots.sens: This word means 'prayer' and comes from the root 'προσεύχομαι' which evokes the idea of an act of devotion and communication with God. This term means 'third' and emphasizes the idea of repetition and insistence. In the context of this verse, it shows Jesus' persistence in prayer, despite fatigue and anguish. This word means 'to say' or 'to speak' and is often used to express important statements. 44.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the 1st century, during the time of the Jewish Passover, a moment of great religious significance for the Jews, marking the liberation from slavery in Egypt.
44.passage: Matthew 26 describes the events leading up to the crucifixion of Jesus, where He withdraws to pray in the Garden of Gethsemane, confronted with the anguish of His redemptive mission. This chapter highlights Jesus' inner struggle and the importance of prayer in this critical moment.
44.culture: In Jewish culture, prayer was a central act of daily life, often associated with moments of crisis or need for divine guidance. Repeated prayers, like those of Jesus, were also a common practice, emphasizing the importance of persistence in faith.

mots.sens: The word 'hypnos' means 'sleep' and evokes a state of inactivity or inattentiveness. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes human weakness in the face of spiritual trials. 45.epoque: This passage is set in the first century, in a context where religious and political tensions were high, particularly between Jewish and Roman authorities.

45.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of spiritual vigilance. While Jesus faces His destiny, His disciples choose rest over prayer, illustrating the human tendency to ignore urgent spiritual realities. This reminds us that in our own lives, we must remain awake and attentive to the moments when God is at work.
45.commentaire: This passage exhorts us to be vigilant in our spiritual life, especially in times of crisis. Like the disciples, we can easily be distracted by comfort and apathy. It is crucial to cultivate a life of prayer and communion with God, so that we remain alert and receptive to His call, especially when times are difficult.

mots.sens: This word means 'to deliver' or 'to hand over.' In the context of Matthew 26:46, it evokes the idea of betraying or handing someone over to an enemy. 46.epoque: This passage is set in the first century, during the Jewish Passover, a crucial moment in Jewish tradition, where sacrifices and rituals are at the heart of the spiritual life of the Jews.
46.passage: Matthew 26 describes the events leading up to the crucifixion of Jesus. This verse marks the moment when Jesus announces that his betrayal is imminent, highlighting the anguish and tension prevailing in the Garden of Gethsemane.
46.culture: In Jewish culture, betrayal is considered one of the worst acts, especially in the context of a master-disciple relationship. The Passover is also a time of reflection on liberation and sacrifice.
46.interpretation: This verse highlights the reality of human betrayal in the face of divine faithfulness. Jesus, aware of his destiny, calls his disciples to rise, symbolizing a call to vigilance and commitment in critical moments.
46.commentaire: Matthew 26:46 reminds us that even in moments of betrayal and suffering, we are called to rise and move forward in faith. Jesus, anticipating his suffering, shows us the importance of spiritual preparation. In our lives, it is essential to remain vigilant and respond to God's call, even when times are difficult.

mots.sens: The name 'Judas' means 'praise' in Hebrew. In this context, it is tragic to see a man whose name evokes praise betray the Master.
